title: Monotonicity of public-coin complexity in the error
statement: Let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ be a function of two arguments, and let $\varepsilon, \varepsilon' \in \bbr$ be error parameters with $\varepsilon' \le \varepsilon$. Then the $\varepsilon$-error public-coin randomized communication complexity of $f$ is at most its $\varepsilon'$-error public-coin randomized communication complexity: $\mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{pub}}_\varepsilon(f) \le \mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{pub}}_{\varepsilon'}(f)$, this inequality holding in $\bbn_\infty$. That is, permitting a larger error tolerance can only decrease the worst-case number of bits that must be exchanged.
hypotheses_covered: f : X → Y → α is a two-argument function
real error parameters ε and ε'
replaced:
Public-coin communication complexity is monotone in the error parameter: if
$\varepsilon' \le \varepsilon$, then
$\mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{pub}}_\varepsilon(f) \le \mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{pub}}_{\varepsilon'}(f)$.
Allowing more error can only make computation easier.
